CHIEF RULING — `importance` NEEDS BOTH CARRIERS. Neither subsumes the other. Answering the question
scout flagged, having read signature.scala:265-274 rather than ruling from the summary.

WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY, and the part that is already right:

    val importance = view.leaves.flatMap(n => n.importance.toOption.map(w => (n.ref, w)))
    val wsum = importance.map(_._2).sum
    if wsum <= 0 then Estimate.missing(MissingReason.AllMissing)
    else Estimate.observed(importance.map { case (r, w) => w * visitation(r) }.sum / wsum)

Leaves whose importance is Missing are EXCLUDED from the weighted sum rather than counted as zero,
and the all-missing case yields Missing rather than republishing the uniform figure. The comment
explains exactly why, and it is the best statement of the estimand principle anywhere in this
codebase: "republishing the UNIFORM figure under the importance-weighted name told a caller that a
salience-weighted measurement had been made when none had. The two fields would then be the same
number under two names, which is the inference a reader cannot help making."

THE DEFECT IS THE PARTIAL CASE, NOT THE EMPTY ONE. If ONE leaf of a hundred carries an importance,
`wsum > 0`, and the field publishes `Observed` -- a salience-weighted coverage figure computed from
one leaf, indistinguishable from the same figure computed from all hundred.

RULING: `wsum` IS THE VALUE'S NORMALIZER, NOT ITS SUPPORT. They are different quantities and
`importance` must carry both:
  - `wsum`, the conditioning mass the value is divided by;
  - `Coverage(eligible = view.leaves.size, observed = importance.size)`, how much of the population
    contributed at all.

NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER, and here is the case that proves it: a large `wsum` from a few heavy
leaves and an identical `wsum` from many light ones are different epistemic situations producing
the same normalizer. Coverage separates them; `wsum` cannot. Equally, coverage alone cannot tell
you whether the contributing leaves carried most of the weight or a sliver of it.

So this is the ADR 0003 shape in its purest form -- a figure published without the support that
says how much of the population it rests on -- and it is the same relationship as
`MassRatio(value, conditioningMass, totalMass)`, which already exists and already carries exactly
this pair. Prefer reusing that shape to inventing a new one.

SCOPE NOTE: this makes `importance` a THIRD distinct shape in the backlog, alongside `uniform`'s
absence-only defect and the external terms' subnormalization trap. It is not the specificity
migration and must not be done by copying it.
